## Development control documents

- docs/node-status-gate-matrix.ko.md / .en.md — READ FIRST at every session start. One-page integrated status board indexing every node: purpose, design status, prerequisite, implementation, build/verify, current verdict, blocker cause, resolution, next gate, and detail links. It is an INDEX, not the source of truth: it links to roadmap, progress, briefs, architecture, build-history, and worklog rather than copying their figures. Uses state values (CLOSED / CONDITIONAL / DEFERRED / NOT ACCEPTED / NOT STARTED) and gates, never progress percentages. Main track A-H and the parallel S track (S0-S8) are separate tables.
- docs/development-roadmap.ko.md / .en.md — authoritative A→B→C development flow; roadmap nodes are not version numbers.
- docs/development-progress.ko.md / .en.md — current node, substep, blocker, validation, and next gate.
- docs/implementation-briefs/B-adaptive-scheduler.ko.md / .en.md — staged Node B implementation contract.
- docs/implementation-briefs/C-calibration-profile.ko.md / .en.md — Node C partial reuse/extension of profile and benchmark concepts.
- docs/implementation-briefs/D-pipeline-queue.ko.md / .en.md — new Node D pipeline/queue implementation contract.
- docs/implementation-briefs/process-backend-isolation-0.9.4.ko.md / .en.md — 0.9.4.x GUI↔Backend process isolation implementation brief: ownership, IPC, lifecycle, watchdog/restart, SQLite authority, recovery semantics, migration boundaries, acceptance gates, and 0.9.5 deferrals.
- docs/implementation-briefs/A-foundation-terminology-instrumentation.ko.md / .en.md - reference contract for the CLOSED Node A (GPU abstraction, ON/OFF only, build naming, MeasureState, decodedFrames/sampledFrames split, and the deprecated items still present in code). Origin evidence: docs/build-history/0.9.4.0.*.
- docs/implementation-briefs/S-validation-benchmark-track.ko.md / .en.md - integrated contract of the parallel S0-S8 validation/benchmark track. Does not replace the per-stage S4/S5/S6 briefs; it states the stage definitions, the standing rules, and the semantic boundary.
- docs/architecture/gui-diagnostic-logging.ko.md / .en.md — authoritative GUI Detailed Logs vs CLI Benchmark semantic boundary.
- docs/implementation-briefs/S4-gui-diagnostic-logging.ko.md / .en.md — current S4 GUI detailed-logging implementation contract.
- docs/architecture/product-acceptance-runbook.ko.md / .en.md — executable checklist for the final Search/Index/Comparison product acceptance (prerequisites, per-area checks with expected evidence, verdict/recording rules, crash-procedure and build-history references).
- docs/implementation-briefs/S4-gui-benchmark-integration.ko.md / .en.md — historical/superseded GUI benchmark execution design, retained for provenance.
- docs/build-history/S4-phase3-4-verification.ko.md / .en.md — S4 Phase 3-4 regression and judgement record: real-engine GUI E2E results plus the unresolved Resource Policy delivery and datasetFingerprint gaps.
- docs/implementation-briefs/S5-console-benchmark-execution.ko.md / .en.md - S5 Console benchmark contract: --benchmark entry, Console renderer, Ctrl+C cancellation, and the five confirmed decisions.
- docs/build-history/S5-verification.ko.md / .en.md - S5 verification record: S5-1/2/3 scope, the Scanner FileState.kind media-scope defect and its one-line fix reusing isVideoPath(), the traced no-impact finding for production indexing/search, real --media/mode/suite/log-dir/log/non-TTY E2E values, CPU 96/96 and GPU 97/97 CTest, two NOT RUN items (real TTY ANSI repaint, real Ctrl+C trigger), and the unfixed S3 localtime-with-Z timestamp mismatch.
- docs/implementation-briefs/S6-data-mining-automation.ko.md / .en.md - S6 design contract, no code yet: verified journal field inventory per eventType, the measured 0-occurrence gaps (git / resourcePolicy / cpuPercent / gpuEnabled / distance) that currently block the roadmap's cross-build comparison, measured/derived/invalid split, replayJournal reuse instead of a new parser, deferred regression threshold, four-way timestamp split and its workaround, S6-1..S6-7 decomposition, entry/exit conditions and deferrals.
- docs/architecture/legacy/S5_REJECTED_CPU_FB_INDICATOR.ko.md / .en.md - REJECTED design record for the Console CPU FB column; never implemented in the product.
- docs/implementation-briefs/S6-measurement-gate.ko.md / .en.md - S6 measurement gate contract, design only with no product code: measured environment and dataset figures, the finding that the current store holds only a 10-file S5 e2e fixture and that CUDA was unavailable because of the CPU build rather than missing hardware, reuse of the already-measured 0.9.4.32 run-to-run variation instead of a new baseline, the crossed A B B A execution order, ModeElapsed as the primary metric with RunWallDuration excluded for its one-second resolution, the warm-cache policy that does not claim OS cache control, and the entry/exit conditions for the S6 verdict layer.
- docs/build-history/<version>.ko.md / .en.md — per-version implementation and validation evidence.
- docs/architecture/database-structure.ko.md / .en.md — current persistent DB structure: `index.sqlite` (files/matches/thumbs/file_trace/content_hash/meta; images+videos shared via files.kind), `video_cache.sqlite` (video_fingerprint_cache, video-only), PRAGMA/WAL, version constants (DB 1.0.6 / engine 1.5.1 / cache 9 / sampling "3"), and the planned pair-verification speedups V-1..V-7 with preliminary verdicts. Links to the measurement record.
- docs/architecture/database-verification-benchmark.ko.md / .en.md — measurement record for the V-1..V-7 pair-verification speedups (plan, conditions, raw values, verdicts; baseline = the 0.9.4.91 log). Unmeasured values are `Not measured`.
- docs/document-naming.ko.md / .en.md — canonical documentation naming, location, and role-separation rules.
- Version progression is evidence-driven: validated states may advance 0.9.4.0 → 0.9.4.1 → 0.9.4.2 without fixed version assignments to roadmap nodes.

## GPU backend direction

The top-level architecture uses GPU as the generic accelerator term. NVIDIA CUDA is one concrete backend, not the generic GPU name. The 0.9.4.x roadmap leaves explicit connection points for NVIDIA CUDA/NVDEC, Vulkan, AMD HIP/ROCm, and Intel Level Zero, covering both integrated and discrete Intel/AMD GPUs. Vulkan is a vendor-neutral candidate; real availability and performance require capability and workload measurement.

## Benchmark / telemetry direction

0.9.4.x treats instrumentation as a first-class architecture layer, but GUI Detailed Logs and CLI Benchmark have different purposes. GUI [상세 로그] is user-workload diagnostic telemetry; CLI --benchmark is controlled development comparison of AUTO / CPU-only / GPU-max. The shared instrumentation boundary is TelemetryRecorder with UserDiagnostic or Benchmark purpose. Unmeasured values must not be written as numeric zero. Detailed design: docs/architecture/benchmark-telemetry-roadmap.ko.md / .en.md and docs/architecture/gui-diagnostic-logging.ko.md / .en.md.

## CPU + GPU execution model

The project is explicitly a CPU+GPU cooperative application.

- CPU is always retained as the reference/fallback execution path.
- Resource Mode is Maximum, High, Balanced, and Minimum (Gaming renamed to Minimum in 0.9.4.96; Custom removed from the GUI).
- Maximum/High/Balanced/Minimum define CPU resource policy.
- Manual defines a user-selected CPU resource limit.
- GPU is ON/OFF only. There is no target architecture for a user-selected GPU utilization percentage.
- GPU ON means Adaptive GPU Scheduler / AUTO workload management.
- CPU/GPU allocation is dynamic and is not fixed at 50:50.
- Scheduler inputs include hardware baseline performance, live CPU/GPU load, queue pressure, measured throughput, decoder capability, and CPU↔GPU transfer cost.
- The first-run or recalibration performance profile is stored in INI and reused as the next scan's initial estimate.
- Live runtime conditions always override stale baseline assumptions.
- Low-end or inefficient GPUs may be assigned little or no work.
- Hardware video decode, including NVDEC, is optional and must retain Software FFmpeg fallback.
- Minimum mode (labeled Gaming before 0.9.4.96) is a conservative adaptive policy for coexistence with external foreground workloads.
- Manual mode constrains CPU resource use while GPU remains AUTO.

Detailed target architecture: docs/architecture/resource-scheduling.ko.md and docs/architecture/resource-scheduling.en.md. Multi-vendor backend roadmap: docs/architecture/gpu-backend-roadmap.ko.md and docs/architecture/gpu-backend-roadmap.en.md.

Important status: 0.9.4.26 implements Nodes A–C plus D1a/D1b observability, D2 completion-order harvest, the D3-Minimal bounded walker queue, D4a CUDA backend internal timing, D8a/D8b the reproducible and scaled dataset (benchmark schemaVersion 8), D9a the analyze internal stage split (schemaVersion 9), the 0.9.4.24 QSettings identity change, 0.9.4.25 D9b Candidate B which is NOT ACCEPTED, and 0.9.4.26 D9c and D9d which are both instrumentation builds. D9c measured where the 8.564 ms expensive verify goes: decode 94.90%, the stat+64 KiB quick-hash key 3.76%, frame_ssim 0.55%, crop/aspect 0.17%, mirror flip 0.16%, other 0.41%, with the seven exclusive stages plus the remainder summing to verifyMs exactly. D9d then decomposed that decode region across 25,898 calls (12,949 decode + 12,949 decodePreserveAspect) at 4.4654 ms per call: open (CreateDecoderFromFilename) 62.15%, factory (per-call WIC COM CoCreateInstance) 27.39%, copy (CopyPixels, which is where WIC actually decompresses) 5.15%, comInit 0.43%, resize/Fant 0.32%, convert 0.27%, EXIF metadata 0.17%, orient 0.01%. So open+factory is 89.54% of decode and 84.9% of the entire expensive verify, while the actual image decompression is a twentieth of it. Three plausible targets were refuted by measurement: WICBitmapInterpolationModeFant (0.32%), EXIF skip (0.17%), and the decompression itself. D9d also settled the question D9c could not: the verify cache's global mutex is NOT a bottleneck, with 40,417 acquires at 0.0002 ms wait and 0.0018 ms hold, i.e. 80.8 ms total or 0.07% of decode, so D9c's `other` bucket holds no hidden contention. decodeSubSumMs trails decodeTotalMs by 4.1% and that gap is reported as unmeasured inter-call code rather than attributed to a stage. All verify counters and groups 156,152 stayed identical to 0.9.4.24 D9a across 5 runs, and D9c's exclusive sum still holds exactly. Two non-measurement items shipped in the same version: the GUI translation keys colFile/colDate/viewGrid were missing from trStr() and rendered as literal "colFile"/"colDate" in the file list header, now fixed with a regression gate; and benchmark schema v9 was confirmed additive-read with a test rather than assumed, which is why kBenchmarkSchemaVersion stayed at 9. Measured on the 2700-file D8b dataset, fingerprint 9b113848…4253c, AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D / RTX 3080 Ti, cold index, 5 runs, 6.3% spread. Because D9c/D9d are instrumented builds, read their stage shares rather than absolute milliseconds. Next is Candidate D1 (decoder construction and file open), which must first decompose the 2.77 ms open and the 1.22 ms factory, and check whether the CLSID_WICImagingFactory2 attempt is falling back. Candidate A stays deferred and frame_ssim stays low priority.

CPU 116/116, GPU 117/117). `0.9.4.72` was the previous build (scan stall fix: walk/analyze parallelization + display/ETR; reproduced with headless `--scan`; walk read ~10.6->~55 MB/s). `0.9.4.71` was (backend defect fixes plus ThumbnailStore: ExecutionPolicy over IPC restores Maximum, Index Complete = analyzed+unchanged, single CPU/RAM summary meaning, slowest-list cacheHit/0ms exclusion, allMatches_ release, ThumbnailStore JPEG end-to-end, fileMeta in-place; the Qt JPEG plugin deployment regression replaced with shared libjpeg-turbo decode; CPU 116/116, GPU 117/117). `0.9.4.70` moved the remaining GUI decoders to FILE_META requests (zero GUI pixel decode; dumpbin Qt6Core-only; §15 all checked, numbers locked). `0.9.4.69` spawned the real Backend process with Supervisor and JSONL IPC (async thumbnails; E2E proves PID split, kill-to-restart, FAILED, DB reopen). `0.9.4.68` routed the GUI through the P2 BackendClient abstraction with in-process Loopback. `0.9.4.67` declared the P1 BackendCore boundary plus Backend entry point. `0.9.4.66` fixed the view-mode overlap (layout pass forced after catch-up icon changes and at switch end; view_mode_probe 18 scenarios 201 checks). `0.9.4.65` made the scan failure handlers non-throwing. `0.9.4.64` folded the display option into the settings dialog general tab (round-trip unchanged; test closer-race fix). `0.9.4.63` added the GUI usability trio (Show Detailed Logs setting, splitter middle-first, filename selectable; - GUI is user-first: Search/Update remains the real execution path; [상세 로그] / [Detailed Logs] is diagnostic telemetry, not a benchmark workflow.
- S4 implementation and visible UI are PASS; functional Detailed Logs acceptance remains DEFERRED.
- S5 infrastructure is REVALIDATED; final product benchmark validation is DEFERRED until the product Search/Index/Comparison acceptance audit is complete.
- The implemented production path is already present: `MainWindow/ScanWorker -> MediaSearchEngine::scan() -> CandidateIndex/ScanPipeline -> image/video verification -> matches/database`.
- Current next gate: S4 real GUI screen acceptance, followed by `color_thumb` R1 (0.9.4.47 candidate), XMP coverage validation, and then meaningful S5 benchmark measurement.

## Repository layout

- The real source tree is src_unpacked/.
- src_unpacked/src/ - engine, pure-C++ common layer (GPU backends are optional behind gpu_backend.h; current concrete backend is NVIDIA CUDA).
- src_unpacked/gui/ - Qt widget application (mainwindow.cpp contains Korean UI string literals).
- src_unpacked/tests/ - CTest tests, named msf_*_test.
- src_unpacked/scripts/ - build_windows_gpu.ps1 (canonical GPU entry point, clean build-windows-gpu tree), build_windows_cpu.ps1, package_portable.ps1, prepare_dataset.ps1 (D8 standard dataset generator). build_windows_cuda.ps1 remains a deprecated alias path; the legacy build-windows-cuda tree is preserved.
- src_unpacked/docs/ - per-build history, architecture notes, STRUCTURE.md, and this file.
- src_unpacked/docs/build-history/0.9.4.26.ko.md / .en.md — D9c expensive verify internal cost accounting: decode 94.90%, frame_ssim 0.55% of the 8.564 ms verify. Instrumentation only, parity held, next candidate is decode decomposition.
- src_unpacked/docs/build-history/0.9.4.25.ko.md / .en.md — D9b Candidate B recorded as NOT ACCEPTED: parity held and counters were identical, but the expensive verify cost did not drop because frame_ssim dominates.
- src_unpacked/docs/build-history/0.9.4.24.ko.md / .en.md — QSettings organization renamed to MediaSimilarityFinder-ui with a safe one-time legacy settings migration.
- src_unpacked/docs/worklog/0.9.4.ko.md / .en.md — cumulative 0.9.4 development-line work log: why D was closed on evidence, which hypothesis was refuted by measurement, what was deliberately left unimplemented, and the working rules learned.
- src_unpacked/docs/recent-work-report.ko.md / .en.md — single-document summary report of the three most recent important changes: the --version console output fix (attachParentConsole stream misdetection), the CUDA C4819 encoding warning removal (-Xcompiler /utf-8 for the CUDA host compiler), and the XMP Orientation Fallback implementation plus its independent review correction and the color_thumb no-FFmpeg audit pre-register. Points at build-history/worklog for the underlying evidence.
- src_unpacked/AGENTS.md - working rules (docs policy, build baseline 0.9.2.32, working validation line 0.9.4.25, CUDA invariance, release procedure).

## Key entry points

- src/media_search_engine.cpp - MediaSearchEngine::scan() orchestrates listing, analysis, candidate indexing, similarity, live streaming of matches, checkpoints, persistence, and the GPU counters (gpuImagesProcessed(), gpuActive()).
- src/scan_pipeline.cpp - duplicate detection. Image pairs via bestMatch/thresholdFor; video full-frame hits match immediately while crop-only hits must pass a duration gate then temporal() + video_crop_similarity({threshold,8,2,2.0}); degenerate hashes (hash_usable) never match.
- src/video_fingerprint.cpp - VideoFingerprintEngine::build() (low-variance frame exclusion, scene-change detection, GPU-batched 32x32 pHash with CPU fallback, currently backed by CUDA, crop fingerprints), video_similarity()/video_crop_similarity() DTW with sceneBonus and dyadic-grid thinning, CUDA row-batched 48x48 MSSIM with CPU fallback; versioned SQLite cache.
- src/database.cpp - primary SQLite index: file fingerprints, persistent matches, and GUI thumbs cache.
- src/video_sampling.cpp - make_sample_plan() sample timestamps by duration; sampling_interval().
- src/image_decoder.cpp / src/media_pipeline.cpp / src/gpu_backend.cpp - image decode and CPU/CUDA hashing.
- gui/mainwindow.cpp - UI, GPU status, persistent thumbnail cache, Pairs/ETR display, preview via Windows shell thumbnail cache first for cached shell entries, then decoders.

## Tests

Current CMake defines 126 CTest registrations; the current configured CPU/GPU Release trees execute 125/125 and 126/126 respectively (0.9.4.144 build). A GUI-less configure (MSF_BUILD_GUI=OFF + MSF_BUILD_TESTS=ON) is supported since 0.9.4.120 and registers the core tests only (98 on the reference machine). These include verify_parity_test (the D9b optimized verify path must be double-identical to the preserved pre-D9b reference), ui_cpu_policy_test (the user-visible CPU control, stored policy, and engine input share the same 10-90 range), ui_detailed_log_test (the S4 execution-strategy controls, the [Detailed Logs] toggle, and the absence of any benchmark run/stop/status workflow), ui_translation_keys_test (any UI string key missing from trStr() renders as its own camelCase identifier because trStr falls back to returning the key; colFile/colDate/viewGrid were missing and showed up that way), benchmark_schema_test (proves benchmark schema v9 is additive-read: the GUI detailed-log dialog is the only structured reader and it does key lookups only, so pre-D9c fields read identically with and without the new fields), thumb_cache_test, video_reencode_test, video_real_test, unicode_video_path_test, video_ssim_test, video_gpu_benchmark_test, video_degenerate_hash_test, video_decode_parity_test, video_scan_e2e_test, scan_pipeline_test, scan_cancel_test, scan_streaming_test, match_store_test, match_revalidate_test, search_engine_test, image_verify_test, quicklook_pipe_test, ui_reference_order_test, fingerprint_fast_test, reveal_window_test, benchmark_test, gpu_timing_test, analyze_telemetry_test, dataset_fingerprint_test, dataset_e2e_test, monitor tests, candidate tests, image/GPU/pipeline tests, and UI state/layout probes. The retired GUI benchmark worker/storage tests live only under docs/architecture/legacy/.

## Build & release

- Build CPU: scripts/build_windows_cpu.ps1 -VcpkgRoot C:\src\vcpkg (VS 2026 x64, project-local vcpkg_installed, vcpkg.json is the single dependency source).
- Build GPU: scripts/build_windows_gpu.ps1 -VcpkgRoot C:\src\vcpkg (canonical; clean build-windows-gpu tree). The legacy build-windows-cuda tree is preserved, not renamed in place.
- Smoke: MediaSimilarityFinder.exe --smoke (offscreen) and --version.
- Performance experiment records: every tuning, profiling, benchmark, microbenchmark, bottleneck analysis, CPU/GPU cost analysis, memory/IO/decode investigation, thread-contention and cache investigation is preserved as a technical record REGARDLESS of whether it succeeded. Refuted hypotheses, measurements, run conditions, refutation reasons and future revisit conditions are all kept. No dedicated docs/experiments/ directory exists by design: the detailed numbers live in the version Build History, and docs/worklog/0.9.4.*.md carries a "Performance / Tuning Experiment Index" linking the experiment lineage (D9a BASELINE -> D9b NOT ACCEPTED -> D9c PASS -> D9d PASS -> D1 PASS) with each surviving, deferred and refuted candidate plus its revisit condition. NOT ACCEPTED / REJECTED / DEFERRED / LOW PRIORITY are verdicts under current conditions, not permanent retirements, and are never deleted. Unmeasured values are written as N/A or Not measured, never estimated. Profiling telemetry is itself a verification target: stage sums must reconstruct the original total. Full field list and status vocabulary: src_unpacked/AGENTS.md item 9 and docs/document-naming.*.md section 2-1.- Source backup: scripts/backup_src.ps1 [-Keep 5] writes backup/MediaSimilarityFinder-v<version>-src.zip containing source + docs. It uses `git archive` only, so the zip is byte-identical to GitHub by construction and can never pick up uncommitted working-tree edits. It refuses to run when HEAD != origin/main or when tracked files are dirty. Keeps the newest 5 and recycles the oldest beyond that. Run it at every version bump; this rule is session- and agent-independent (AGENTS.md item 4).
- Portable backup: scripts/package_portable.ps1 collects the exe, Qt/runtime DLLs, ffmpeg/ffprobe and the VC++ CRT, runs a `--smoke` test, and writes backup/MediaSimilarityFinder-v<version>-Portable-Windows-x64.zip. It is a build artifact and is never committed. Both zip kinds live together in the repository-root backup/ folder and each rotates independently at 5.
- Version bump files: CMakeLists.txt, vcpkg.json, gui/main.cpp (kVersion), scripts/package_portable.ps1, src/index_manager.cpp.
- CI workflows under .github/workflows/ are manual-dispatch regression workflows aligned with VS2026, src_unpacked, and project-local vcpkg_installed. The hosted CUDA workflow validates CUDA compilation and device-independent tests; local NVIDIA hardware remains the runtime validation authority.

## URLs

Use raw GitHub URLs for source files when programmatic access is needed.

## Active-node document hierarchy

Read in this order before changing source: Node Status / Gate Matrix -> Roadmap -> Progress -> the active node's Implementation Brief -> relevant architecture -> build-history / worklog -> source / test.

Roadmap = direction and dependency order. Progress = actual state and recovery history. Implementation Brief = focused engineering contract for the active node. Build History = version-specific evidence. Node Status / Gate Matrix = one-page index of node state, prerequisite, blocker, verdict, and next gate.

Current design classification: B and D are new design work; C is partial reuse + extension.
